judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain within Class IX (both coordinate rank 0), under the same Chapter 'Diversity in living organisms' and Content Domain 'The World of the Living', but they hang from different NCERT LO parents (CLO49 under LO14 'draws conclusions'; CLO48 under LO11 'applies learning to hypothetical situations'). CLO48 asks learners to apply characteristic/salient features and classification parameters to hypothetical scenarios (e.g. reptilians becoming amphibians), while CLO49 asks learners to draw conclusions connecting larger principles of classification with the process of evolution. Both resolved Class coordinates are 'Class IX' (rank 0), so buildsTowards would require substantive same-rank developmental evidence. The bounded evidence shows genuine conceptual coherence — the particulate description of solid/liquid/gas (shape, intermolecular spaces, continuous particle movement) and the recognition of evaporation in everyday processes (drying of clothes, cooling of surfaces) are complementary parts of the same chapter's account of matter and change of state, and the Learning Components ('differentiates between the three states of matter...', 'relates the drying of clothes / cooling of surfaces to the process of evaporation') reinforce that shared conceptual territory. producer_judgment.rationale: Both are Class IX Indicators (same statement-type grain) in Chapter 1 'Matter in our surroundings', Content Domain 'Materials'. Indicator C4 establishes differentiation of the three states of matter in terms of shape, intermolecular spaces and continuous particle movement (under CLO1 'Differentiates the three states of matter'), i.e. the particulate model of matter. Indicator C10 applies that model to everyday phenomena, relating drying of clothes and cooling of surfaces to evaporation (under CLO4 'Applies the concept of evaporation seen in day-to-day life'; NCERT LO12 on applying concepts in daily life). Although both sit at the same Class IX rank, the pair-specific evidence shows a conceptual-to-application move: proficiency in explaining liquid/gas states via particle spacing and motion supports success in explaining and identifying evaporation in daily-life situations, whereas the reverse support is not evidenced. Token/trigram and page-proximity signals are weak stopword-level overlap and were not treated as semantic support; source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, so the judgment rests on the supplied statement texts, codes, parent CLO/LO texts, and table row placement.
